doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

chapter: Growing up with his father and Joe Morello
title: Joe Morello around the house and as a taskmaster
summary: Morello visited his father, tested him on his left hand, and later gave him lessons in New Jersey.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well you’ve had a relationship with Joe Morello over the years. Can you tell me about him a little bit?

Well he was around the house quite a bit when I was growing up, because he was friends with my dad. And when he was traveling with the quartet he used to come home to his family and inevitably stop by and see my father, and talk about the road and what was going on and give the latest album to my dad, autographed. And I can remember when he came up with “Rondo a la Turk.” That was something else that — what do you think of this — and you know my father would say, “You’re playing terrible.” Constantly put him

on and they would put one another on constantly, so I was exposed to him. And when he came through, he would ask me, “Well how’s your left hand?” You know, how’s this going, how’s this going, and listen to me a little bit, and forget about it. And he was a task master. And he wanted the student that really wanted it. You couldn’t just have an interest in music, you have to want it, and I wanted it, and I kept coming back to it. And then I asked him, “Well listen to this now.” And eventually I went down to New Jersey and took some lessons with him. But a big influence, one of my favorite drummers of all time. A master, a legend.
